unit.why: A hospitality tale about R. Abish, Av Beit Din of Frankfurt, a non-Hasidic rabbinic figure. It is followed by an interpretation the author heard from his father in the name of the Seer of Lublin.

stories.start_quote: בהיות הה״ג ר׳ אביש אב״ד בפפד״מ
stories.end_quote: שיאמינו בדברי חז״ל וד״ל. (ברכת אברהם בהק')
stories.summary_en: A repulsive guest at R. Abish's Sabbath table devours everything, rages and curses him, and demands more. R. Abish patiently feeds him, even slaughtering thirteen oxen, until the guest reveals he came to test whether R. Abish would lose his temper. The Seer of Lublin explains that the real test was R. Abish's faith in the sages' dictum that a poor man is hungry.

tags.why: Praises the patience and faith of R. Abish of Frankfurt, a non-Hasidic rabbi
Placed under the heading on hospitality as an exemplary tale
